findings.summary: Round 3's 124-attribution major was fixed in backlog.md ONLY. All three javadoc sites round 3 named by line number still say the whole 124 'write the lease' and still name the ambiguous arm as their cause -- and now contradict this same commit's backlog cell.
findings.detail: Round-3 finding f13bb531d5dc #2 cited docs/internal/product/backlog.md:38 AND, verbatim in its detail, GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:222 ('**124 windows per 1,000 seeds already write the lease and then throw**. That is the injected ambiguous putIfMatch'), :264 ('the mechanism behind the sweep's 124 windows') and :271 ('the 124 windows would stop being counted at all'). backlog.md:38 now reads correctly -- '124 windows ... move the verb counter and THEN THROW ... NOT ONE ARM, AND NOT ALL OF THEM WROTE ANYTHING ... refuseIfPartitioned (nothing reaches the delegate at all) ... the withheldPut arm (whose own comment says the version does not move)'. The javadocs did not move: GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:221-225 still reads 'so **124 windows per 1,000 seeds already write the lease and then throw**. That is the injected ambiguous {@code putIfMatch}', :300-302 'That is the mechanism behind the sweep's 124 windows per 1,000 seeds', :306-308 'the 124 windows would stop being counted at all'. Verified against the code once more: FaultInjectingStore.putIfMatch (FaultInjectingStore.java:594-643) records at the top and throws from three places -- refuseIfPartitioned at :624 (nothing reaches the delegate), the ambiguousPut arm (write lands), the withheldPut arm at :634-641 whose own comment says 'THE VERSION DOES NOT MOVE'. Both non-ambiguous arms are enabled in SWEEP_FAULTS (CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:97, withheldPut 0.02, partitionRate 0.02), and the 38 measured refusal windows are inside the 124 writing nothing -- which the backlog cell now states and the javadoc still denies. Two staged files in one commit now assert opposite things about the same number. Failure scenario: a later hand tightening the sweep reads the TEST -- the copy a reader of the meter hits first -- as saying 124 ambiguous landings per 1,000 seeds, floors an ambiguous-landing counter near 124 (the tree reaches roughly half that), and it reds with no defect present; or carries :227's gloss ('the lease really is expired on the store, so a successor does not wait out the TTL') across all 124 when in the withheld and partition windows the version never moved and the successor waits the full TTL. Fix is the same clause round 3 named, applied at the three sites it named: say ambiguous-landing PLUS refused PLUS withheld, or drop the attribution.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand tightening the sweep reads GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:222 -- the copy a reader of the meter hits first -- as saying the 1,000-seed run produces 124 ambiguous landings, and floors an ambiguous-landing counter near 124. The tree can only reach roughly half that (the rest are the 38 partition refusals, which write nothing, plus the withheldPut arm, whose own comment says the version does not move), so the new floor reds with no defect present. The same reader carries :227's 'the lease really is expired on the store, so a successor does not wait out the TTL' across all 124 windows, when in the refused and withheld ones the version never moved and the successor waits the full TTL.

findings.summary: M5.35's new `writesBefore = 0` evidence was appended to the SERVES column, not the Task cell -- an 818-character requirement ID, unique in the file (next longest is 29 chars).
findings.detail: The table header at backlog.md:25 is `| ID | Task | Serves | State |`. The M5.35 row's cells after this diff are: ID ' M5.35 ', Task (2,156 chars), Serves (818 chars, beginning 'FR-11 ⚠️ AND M5.29 ADDED A THIRD OF THE SAME FAMILY...'), State ' todo '. Every other Serves cell in the file is an ID or an em dash; the only other one over 12 characters is M3.0's 'FR-18 (byte reservation only)' at 29. The diff introduced this: the old row ended '... never observed across windows | FR-11 | todo |'. Consequence, and it is not cosmetic: a person picking up M5.35 reads the Task cell, which still lists exactly two mutations, (a) and (b). The third -- `int writesBefore = 0` at the top of `observe`, the one this row itself calls 'STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE OTHER TWO' because the sweep does not catch it and it 'restores exactly the blindness M5.29 exists to remove' -- is in the requirement column, where task content is not looked for. M5.35 can be implemented, killing (a) and (b), and marked done with the worst of the three alive. Separately, the Serves column is the FR/NFR traceability column: any reader or future check-cross-refs.sh matching a Serves cell against the requirement list gets a paragraph rather than an ID, and the rendered GFM column blows out -- the table-shape family M0.105 spent a commit repairing by hand and M0.109 exists to gate. Fix is moving one cell boundary: the new prose belongs at the end of the Task cell, before ' | FR-11 | todo |'.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever takes M5.35 reads its Task cell -- the cell task content lives in -- and finds exactly two mutations, (a) the kind-guard `continue;`->`break;` and (b) the deleted `break;` after `refusedForAnotherPod++`. They kill both, mark M5.35 done, and `int writesBefore = 0` stays alive: the row's own text calls it 'STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE OTHER TWO' because the sweep does not catch it and, composed with the production swap, it 'restores exactly the blindness M5.29 exists to remove'. The evidence naming it is sitting in the Serves column, which is read for an FR/NFR ID and nothing else.

findings.summary: Both coverage counts written this round are stale by one against the tests this same diff adds: 'Two T1 cases now pin it' (three do) and M5.49's 'Three tests now pin that' (four do).
findings.detail: backlog.md:38 ends '... Two T1 cases now pin it', where 'it' is the `completed` conjunct. Dropping `completed` from GracefulReleaseMeter.java:62 reds THREE cases, not two: aReleaseWhoseWriteLANDEDButTHREWIsNOTCredited (GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:236), theStoresOWNAmbiguousWriteIsCOUNTEDAndStillNotCredited (:311) and aConditionalWriteREFUSEDByAPartitionIsStillCOUNTED (:274) -- the last asserts released() is zero while calls('putIfMatch') is 1, so it reds identically. backlog.md:64 (M5.49) is the same shape one round on: round 3 found 'Two tests ... for stat and putIfMatch' undercounting by one, the cell now says 'Three tests now pin that -- for stat, putIfMatch and list', and this round added a FOURTH position pin -- aConditionalWriteREFUSEDByAPartitionIsStillCOUNTED, which is the second putIfMatch pin (record above refuseIfPartitioned, where theStoresOWNAmbiguousWrite... pins record above the ambiguous throw). The three verbs named are right; the numeral is not. Failure scenario is round 3's, unchanged: whoever takes M5.49 reads 'three tests, one per verb', treats the second putIfMatch case as redundant with the first and deletes it, and putIfMatch -- the verb the meter actually credits -- loses its only pin of `record` above `refuseIfPartitioned`, which is the exact half the new test's own javadoc says round 3 left open ('Closing one of two is the failure mode this commit has now recorded twice').
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever takes M5.49 reads 'Three tests now pin that -- for stat, putIfMatch and list' as one test per verb, finds two putIfMatch cases, treats aConditionalWriteREFUSEDByAPartitionIsStillCOUNTED as redundant with theStoresOWNAmbiguousWriteIsCOUNTEDAndStillNotCredited, and deletes it once the presence grep lands. putIfMatch -- the verb the meter actually credits -- then has no pin of `record` above `refuseIfPartitioned`, so moving the call below the partition check survives again. That is precisely the half the deleted test's own javadoc says round 3 left open.
